checks: For u,v>0 the point (u+v,−u) has x+y=v and (0,−β) has x+y=−β. Their convex segment crosses x+y=0 at interpolation fraction β/(β+v) from (0,−β), with positive x-coordinate β(u+v)/(β+v). The positive diagonal chord endpoint bounds this by ρ. Multiplication by β+v>0 gives βu+(β−ρ)v≤βρ.

The coordinate change has absolute determinant one. For β>ρ the two positive intercepts are ρ and βρ/(β−ρ), so the closed triangle has area βρ²/[2(β−ρ)]. If the closed sector is a proper closed subset of that triangle, its relatively open complement meets the interior and has positive area. Conversely, the closed sector can differ from the original sector only on the two coordinate axes by closedness of K.

For the attaining disk intersection, the defining halfplane contains a neighborhood of zero. Substitution of v=−u on the negative y-axis gives ρu≤βρ, and substitution of v=0 gives u≤ρ. A centered disk containing both endpoints preserves both cutoffs. For β>ρ choose a disk containing the triangle as well, which makes the sector closure that triangle.

For β=ρ or β<ρ the halfplane contains every (u,v) with 0<u<ρ and v>0. The disk intersections contain rectangles of arbitrarily large area in that strip as the radius grows. Each intersection is a compact convex body with the same fixed endpoint pair.
